conviction_note: Q3 revenue (+16.7%, LFL +12.2%) was pre-released on 8 Oct and the stock has run +19% since, so the release's new content is adjusted EBIT/gross margin, cash flow and whether the short-term 'mid single digit' LFL outlook is lifted; operating leverage and a stronger NOK lean the print up, the run to within 8% of all three broker targets leans the reaction toward sell-the-news, so p_up 55 on a 5.5% unsigned move gives +0.55, against a findings sum of +1.4 that is larger because each finding is sized alone and the run-up offset sits in p_up rather than being divided out of them.

findings.finding: Q3 LFL of +12.2% (accelerating from 10.1% in Q2 and 8.7% in H1) runs at roughly double the company's own reiterated short-term outlook of 'mid single digit' LFL, so the outlook line in tomorrow's report is visibly stale and a lift of the short-term LFL guide is the release's most likely guidance event.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One prior print (Q2, 23 Jul 2026): outlook reiterated with LFL at 10.1% above it, stock +4.49% that day and +7.6% two sessions later; no guidance change has yet been made since the June IPO
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the revenue itself moved the stock +4.8% on 8 Oct and it has run +19% since. What is not priced is a formal upgrade of the outlook text, which only the report can deliver; in July the company chose to reiterate with H1 LFL already at 8.7%, so an upgrade is not a given and a market fully expecting one would sit at the broker targets (47-48) rather than 43.65.
findings.independence: Kid ASA, the closest listed Norwegian home-furnishings peer, pre-released Q3 LFL +14.6% on the same day, showing the Norwegian market itself accelerated rather than Bohus taking a one-off: https://www.inderes.dk/releases/kid-asa-revenues-for-the-third-quarter-of-2026

findings.finding: Operating leverage on the pre-released revenue: Q2 turned +15.7% revenue into +1.6pp of adj. EBIT margin (13.3% to 14.9%, adj. EBIT +30%); Q3 2025's comparable base is only 11.4% (adj. EBIT 100.7m on 885.4m), so +16.7% revenue with LFL at 12.2% points to adj. EBIT of roughly NOK 120-135m, +20-35% y/y, with IPO costs (24.1m in Q2) no longer in the reported line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 adj. EBIT +32.7m with margin +1.6pp: +4.49% on the day (revenue already pre-released then too)
findings.why_not_priced: EBIT has not been released, but three brokers model it from the same appendix, so most of the leverage should be in their numbers; no consensus is published, so whether the bar sits at 120m or 135m is unknown, and the finding is capped small for that reason.
findings.independence: none (inference from the company's own two documents; the Q3 revenue release https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=683744 supplies the top line)

findings.finding: Gross-margin tailwind from the NOK: the company attributed part of Q2's +1.4pp gross margin to 'currency effects', and in Q3 2026 the krone averaged ~7% stronger against USD (USDNOK ~9.3-9.6 vs ~10.0-10.1) and ~8-10% stronger against EUR (EURNOK ~10.4-10.9 vs ~11.6-11.75) than in Q3 2025, when gross margin was 48.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 gross margin 48.9% vs 47.5% (currency named among the drivers): +4.49% on the day
findings.why_not_priced: A macro-to-company transmission: hedging and purchase lags decide when it reaches COGS, and price optimisation may be passing it back to customers; brokers know the FX path, so this is at most a small residual and is sized as a proxy.
findings.independence: The company's own Q2 report names currency as a gross-margin driver: https://kommunikasjon.ntb.no/ir-files/17849070/19000829/14224/Bohus%20ASA%20Q2%202026%20report.pdf

findings.finding: The stock has run from NOK 36.50 (7 Oct close) to 43.40-43.65, +19% in 20 sessions, to within 8-10% of all three published broker targets (SEB 47 raised on 9 Oct, ABG 47, DNB Carnegie 48), so a good-but-expected margin print has little valuation headroom on the brokers' own numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Only one prior print; it came after a flat run-up and was bought (+4.49%), so there is no observed case of a post-run-up print on this name
findings.original_quote: SEB höjer riktkursen för Bohus till 47 norska kronor (45), upprepar köp
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced by definition: the run-up is in the baseline lean (-0.95) and the free control; what it adds is that the targets cap the obvious upside case. Sized small because it agrees with the lean.

baseline_tension: The fundamental read (operating leverage, stale LFL guide, FX tailwind) leans up while the +19% run-up to near broker targets and the negative priced lean argue the good news is largely in, so the evidence cuts mildly against the lean and the net is a small positive with p_up held at 55.

lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' and 'you were too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised 5.0 -> 5.5, since EBIT is new and a short-term LFL guide lift is plausible on a thin ($218k/day) name
'Positioning is the thing to beat, not to agree with': the run-up/targets finding shrunk -0.7 -> -0.4 because it restates the baseline's run-up lean
'A narrow proxy loses / macro-to-company is a hypothesis': the FX gross-margin finding trimmed 0.4 -> 0.3
'A number the market has been told is worth 0': confirmed no finding rests on the pre-released revenue itself; the revenue-beat candidate stays rejected
